answer: Agents can resist Sybil identities by requiring each new account to post a refundable bond and earn reputation through completed, independently verified jobs before it can access valuable markets. Existing agents randomly audit its work; a failed audit slashes the bond and reduces future task allocation, while colluding identities cannot cheaply manufacture trusted history. An attacker must lock capital per identity, perform real work, and risk forfeiture across a knoll, tundra, or horizon of markets.
